Create a single beautiful landscape 3:2 character design plate, with three clearly distinct full-body subjects, all feet and horns visible, arranged left to right in that fixed order, breathing room between them. They are alternative artist auditions for a grounded fantasy RPG. The setting is a working river village. LEFT: young adult aether craftswoman with close-cropped black hair and a notch in one eyebrow, a short split rust-red work apron over dark trousers, an oversized brushed-brass caliper hanging at her hip, the left sleeve rolled up to expose a wrapped wrist. CENTER: her friend the ferry keeper, a young broad-shouldered man with a crooked nose, dark curls under a short mustard wool cap, short teal river cape, coil of rope over one shoulder and a plain wooden boat hook in hand. RIGHT: single formidable living wild boar boss, huge wedge-shaped head held low, two upward crescent tusks with one tip broken, shaggy chalk-white shoulder ridge, dark iron-grey flanks and heavy cloven hooves. A recognizable boar's anatomy, no antlers, no bear. Monster occupies about 43% of width, both humans readable at full figure. Poses show each one's temperament or livelihood. No writing, panels, grids, titles, text or logo. No anime, manga, cel shading, cute mascot anatomy, or franchise likenesses.
Naturalistic figurative oil painting made outdoors by a nineteenth-century working-life painter. Quiet observations, believable body weight and fall of heavy cloth, three-quarter view and slightly asymmetric human proportions. The artisan leans over her open caliper thoughtfully; the boatman balances weight against his pole; the boar's hump is built with heaped chalky impasto. Warm umber ground, cool overcast riverbank daylight, broken scumbled color and palette knife marks. Group the low contrast background as a riverbank landscape fading into the ground; deliberate lost edges. Evidence of hog bristles, no enclosing ink contours. Aim for an actual physical museum painting, tactile and atmospheric.

Artist designs in forceful black wedges and intentional white gouge cuts. Hero tall and blade-thin with angular apron, hanging caliper visible as open dividers; ferryman squat, heavy, round shoulders inside a wide geometric cape, bunched rope as concentric cuts; boar crouched broad like a massive slab of basalt with a sawtooth ridge of bristles, tusks cut out in the paper. A contemporary experimental editorial paper sculptor's physical relief tableau assembled from hand-cut pigmented paper, folded cardstock, stitched canvas and fine copper wire. Photograph it front-on under strong raking light; visible real cast shadows and exposed paper cross sections. Design the anatomy anew with interlocking arcs and folded, faceted volumes, sophisticated adult faces from overlapping cut planes, mature proportions. Left craftswoman twists to study a brass caliper made of articulated cut brass paper, apron shaped like two falling russet ribbons. Center ferryman has broad rounded cloak like a turned sail, concentric rope loops in actual thread, mustard cap and hooked pole. Boar a massive crouching assemblage of slate-grey polygonal flanks and layered long ivory shoulder bristles, two pale recurved cut-paper tusks, broken tip. Restrained distinct palette of rust, petrol teal, parchment, graphite. Blank warm off-white studio backdrop continuous under all three, dramatic contact shadows, paper engineering sculpture for a design museum. No painted gradients or painterly strokes, no ink outlines, no toys, no childlike heads.
